Detailed Description

Class to encapsulate the functionality for processing the fparser2 AST and
convert the nodes to PSyIR.

:param ignore_directives: Whether directives should be ignored or not
    (default True). Only has an effect if comments were not ignored when
    creating the fparser2 AST.
:param last_comments_as_codeblocks: Whether the last comments in the a
    given block (e.g. subroutine, do, if-then body, etc.) should be kept as
    CodeBlocks or lost (default False). Only has an effect if comments
    were not ignored when creating the fparser2 AST.
:param resolve_modules: Whether to resolve modules while parsing a file,
    for more precise control it also accepts a list of module names.
    Defaults to False.

:raises TypeError: if the constructor argument is not of the expected type.

staticprotected 
Ensure that the datatype of the symbol with the supplied name has a
pointer or target attribute and if not, add the target attribute.

The datatype is stored as text within an UnsupportedFortranType. We
therefore re-create the datatype as an fparser2 ast, add the attribute
if required and update the UnsupportedFortranType with the new text.

:param str var_name: the name of the symbol for which we attempt to
                     modify the datatype.
:param table: a SymbolTable in which to search for the symbol.
:type table: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.SymbolTable`

:raises NotImplementedError: if the variable cannot be found, is
    unresolved or is not a DataSymbol.
:raises NotImplementedError: if the variable needs to be given
    the target attribute but represents a symbol defined externally
    (e.g. a routine argument or an imported symbol).

3015 def _allocate_handler(self, node, parent):
3016 '''
3017 Transforms an fparser2 Allocate_Stmt into its PSyIR form.
3018
3019 :param node: node in fparser2 tree.
3020 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Allocate_Stmt`
3021 :param parent: parent node of the PSyIR node we are constructing.
3022 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Schedule`
3023
3024 :returns: PSyIR representation of an allocate.
3025 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.IntrinsicCall`
3026
3027 :raises NotImplementedError: if the allocate has a type specification \
3028 (e.g. allocate(character(len=10) :: my_var)).
3029
3030 '''
3031 call = IntrinsicCall(IntrinsicCall.Intrinsic.ALLOCATE, parent=parent)
3032
3033 type_spec = node.children[0]
3034 if type_spec:
3035 raise NotImplementedError(
3036 "Allocate statements with type specifications cannot be "
3037 "handled in the PSyIR")
3038
3039 alloc_list = node.children[1].children
3040 # Loop over each 'Allocation' in the 'Allocation_List'
3041 for alloc in alloc_list:
3042 # Currently fparser produces an incorrect parse tree if 'mold' is
3043 # specified - there is no Allocate object, just the bare Name or
3044 # Data_Ref. This is the subject of fparser/#383.
3045 if isinstance(alloc, (Fortran2003.Name, Fortran2003.Data_Ref)):
3046 # If the allocate() has a 'mold' argument then its positional
3047 # argument(s) is/are just references without any shape
3048 # information.
3049 self.process_nodes(parent=call, nodes=[alloc])
3050 else:
3051 # We have an Allocation(name, Allocate_Shape_Spec_List)
3052 self.process_nodes(parent=call,
3053 nodes=[alloc.children[0]])
3054 cursor = call.children[-1]
3055 while hasattr(cursor, "member"):
3056 cursor = cursor.member
3057 if isinstance(cursor, Member):
3058 # Convert Member to ArrayMember.
3059 aref = ArrayMember(cursor.name)
3060 else:
3061 # Convert Reference to ArrayReference.
3062 aref = ArrayReference(cursor.symbol)
3063 cursor.replace_with(aref)
3064 # Handle the index expressions (each of which is represented
3065 # by an Allocate_Shape_Spec).
3066 for shape_spec in walk(alloc,
3067 Fortran2003.Allocate_Shape_Spec):
3068 self.process_nodes(parent=aref, nodes=[shape_spec])
3069
3070 # Handle any options to the allocate()
3071 opt_list = walk(node, Fortran2003.Alloc_Opt)
3072 for opt in opt_list:
3073 self.process_nodes(parent=call, nodes=opt.children[1:])
3074 call.append_named_arg(opt.children[0], call.children[-1].detach())
3075
3076 # Point to the original statement in the parse tree.
3077 call.ast = node
3078
3079 return call
3080

3081 def _allocate_shape_spec_handler(self, node, parent):
3082 '''
3083 Creates a Range node describing the supplied Allocate_Shape_Spec.
3084 This is similar to the subscript_triplet handler except that the
3085 default lower bound is unity and the step is also unity.
3086
3087 :param node: node in fparser2 AST.
3088 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Allocate_Shape_Spec`
3089 :param parent: parent node of the PSyIR node we are constructing.
3090 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Reference`
3091
3092 :returns: PSyIR of fparser2 node.
3093 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Range`
3094
3095 '''
3096 my_range = Range(parent=parent)
3097 my_range.children = []
3098 integer_type = default_integer_type()
3099
3100 if node.children[0]:
3101 self.process_nodes(parent=my_range, nodes=[node.children[0]])
3102 else:
3103 # Default lower bound in Fortran is 1
3104 my_range.addchild(Literal("1", integer_type))
3105
3106 self.process_nodes(parent=my_range, nodes=[node.children[1]])
3107
3108 # Step is always 1.
3109 my_range.addchild(Literal("1", integer_type))
3110
3111 return my_range

4175 def _array_syntax_to_indexed(self, parent, loop_vars):
4176 '''
4177 Utility function that modifies bare References to arrays as
4178 ArrayReferences, and each ArrayReference that is not inside an
4179 elemental call to use the provided loop index.
4180
4181 :param parent: root of PSyIR sub-tree to search for Array
4182 references to modify.
4183 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
4184 :param loop_vars: the variable names for the array indices.
4185 :type loop_vars: list of str
4186
4187 :raises NotImplementedError: if array sections of differing ranks are
4188 found.
4189 '''
4190 # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
4191 from psyclone.psyir.transformations import (
4192 Reference2ArrayRangeTrans, TransformationError)
4193 # Convert References to arrays to use the array range notation unless
4194 # they have an IntrinsicCall parent.
4195 for ref in parent.walk(Reference):
4196 if isinstance(ref.symbol.interface, (ImportInterface,
4197 UnresolvedInterface)):
4198 raise NotImplementedError(
4199 "PSyclone doesn't yet support reference to imported "
4200 "symbols inside WHERE clauses.")
4201 call_ancestor = ref.ancestor(Call)
4202 if (isinstance(ref.symbol, DataSymbol) and not call_ancestor):
4203 try:
4204 Reference2ArrayRangeTrans().apply(ref)
4205 except TransformationError:
4206 pass
4207 elif (isinstance(ref.symbol, DataSymbol) and call_ancestor
4208 is not None and call_ancestor.is_elemental):
4209 try:
4210 Reference2ArrayRangeTrans().apply(ref)
4211 except TransformationError:
4212 pass
4213 table = parent.scope.symbol_table
4214 one = Literal("1", INTEGER_TYPE)
4215 arrays = parent.walk(ArrayMixin)
4216
4217 first_rank = None
4218 for array in arrays:
4219 # Check that this is a supported array reference and that
4220 # all arrays are of the same rank
4221 rank = len([child for child in array.indices if
4222 isinstance(child, Range)])
4223 if rank == 0:
4224 # This is an array reference without any ranges so we can
4225 # ignore it.
4226 continue
4227
4228 # If it has a Call ancestor we need to check if its a
4229 # non-elemental function, in which case we should skip
4230 # changing it.
4231 call_ancestor = array.ancestor(Call)
4232 if call_ancestor:
4233 if call_ancestor.is_elemental is None:
4234 raise NotImplementedError(
4235 f"Found a function call inside a where clause with "
4236 f"unknown elemental status: "
4237 f"{call_ancestor.debug_string()}")
4238 # If it is none-elemental, we leave this array reference as it
4239 # is
4240 if not call_ancestor.is_elemental:
4241 continue
4242 # Otherwise, we continue replacing the range with the loop idx
4243
4244 if first_rank:
4245 if rank != first_rank:
4246 raise NotImplementedError(
4247 f"Found array sections of differing ranks within a "
4248 f"WHERE construct: array section of {array.name} has "
4249 f"rank {rank}")
4250 else:
4251 first_rank = rank
4252
4253 base_ref = _copy_full_base_reference(array)
4254 array_ref = array.ancestor(Reference, include_self=True)
4255 if not isinstance(array_ref.datatype, ArrayType):
4256 raise NotImplementedError(
4257 f"We can not get the resulting shape of the expression: "
4258 f"{array_ref.debug_string()}")
4259 shape = array_ref.datatype.shape
4260 add_op = BinaryOperation.Operator.ADD
4261 sub_op = BinaryOperation.Operator.SUB
4262 # Replace the PSyIR Ranges with appropriate index expressions.
4263 range_idx = 0
4264 for idx, child in enumerate(array.indices):
4265 if not isinstance(child, Range):
4266 continue
4267 # We need the lower bound of the appropriate dimension of this
4268 # array as we will index relative to it. Note that the 'shape'
4269 # of the datatype only gives us extents, not the lower bounds
4270 # of the declaration or slice.
4271 if isinstance(shape[range_idx], ArrayType.Extent):
4272 # We don't know the bounds of this array so we have
4273 # to query using LBOUND.
4274 lbound = IntrinsicCall.create(
4275 IntrinsicCall.Intrinsic.LBOUND,
4276 [base_ref.copy(),
4277 ("dim", Literal(str(idx+1), INTEGER_TYPE))])
4278 else:
4279 if array.is_full_range(idx):
4280 # The access to this index is to the full range of
4281 # the array.
4282 lbound = array.get_lbound_expression(idx)
4283 else:
4284 # We need the lower bound of this access.
4285 lbound = child.start.copy()
4286
4287 # Create the index expression.
4288 symbol = table.lookup(loop_vars[range_idx])
4289 if isinstance(lbound, Literal) and lbound.value == "1":

4291 # directly.
4292 expr2 = Reference(symbol)
4293 else:
4294 # We don't know what the lower bound is so have to
4295 # have an expression:
4296 # idx-expr = array-lower-bound + loop-idx - 1
4297 expr = BinaryOperation.create(
4298 add_op, lbound, Reference(symbol))

4300 # Indices of an AoSReference start at index 1

5169 def _call_handler(self, node, parent):
5170 '''Transforms an fparser2 CALL statement into a PSyIR Call node.
5171
5172 :param node: node in fparser2 parse tree.
5173 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Call_Stmt`
5174 :param parent: parent node of the PSyIR node we are constructing.
5175 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
5176
5177 :returns: PSyIR representation of node.
5178 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Call`
5179
5180 :raises GenerationError: if the symbol associated with the
5181 name of the call is an unsupported type.
5182
5183 '''
5184 call = Call(parent=parent)
5185 # TODO fparser/#447 For now `null()` is treated as a
5186 # `Function_Reference` by fparser, instead of an
5187 # `Intrinsic_Function_Reference` so we redirect to the correct
5188 # handler for fparser2 tests to pass. This should be removed once
5189 # fparser2 is fixed.
5190 if str(node.items[0]).lower() == "null" and node.items[1] is None:
5191 return self._intrinsic_handler(node, parent)
5192
5193 self.process_nodes(parent=call, nodes=[node.items[0]])
5194 routine = call.children[0]
5195 # If it's a plain reference, promote the symbol to a RoutineSymbol
5196 # pylint: disable=unidiomatic-typecheck
5197 if type(routine) is Reference:
5198 routine_symbol = routine.symbol
5199 if type(routine_symbol) is Symbol:
5200 # Specialise routine_symbol from a Symbol to a
5201 # RoutineSymbol
5202 routine_symbol.specialise(RoutineSymbol)
5203 elif isinstance(routine_symbol, RoutineSymbol):
5204 # This symbol is already the expected type
5205 pass
5206 else:
5207 raise GenerationError(
5208 f"Expecting the symbol '{routine_symbol.name}', to be of "
5209 f"type 'Symbol' or 'RoutineSymbol', but found "
5210 f"'{type(routine_symbol).__name__}'.")
5211
5212 return self._process_args(node, call)

3908 def _case_construct_handler(self, node, parent):
3909 '''
3910 Transforms an fparser2 Case_Construct to the PSyIR representation.
3911
3912 :param node: node in fparser2 tree.
3913 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Case_Construct`
3914 :param parent: parent node of the PSyIR node we are constructing.
3915 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
3916
3917 :returns: PSyIR representation of node
3918 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.IfBlock`
3919
3920 :raises InternalError: If the fparser2 tree has an unexpected
3921 structure.
3922 :raises NotImplementedError: If the fparser2 tree contains an
3923 unsupported structure and should be placed in a CodeBlock.
3924
3925 '''
3926 # Check that the fparser2 parsetree has the expected structure
3927 if len(walk(node, Fortran2003.Select_Case_Stmt)) == 0:
3928 raise InternalError(
3929 f"Failed to find opening case statement in: {node}")
3930 if len(walk(node, Fortran2003.End_Select_Stmt)) == 0:
3931 raise InternalError(
3932 f"Failed to find closing case statement in: {node}")
3933
3934 # Search for all the CASE clauses in the Case_Construct. We do this
3935 # because the fp2 parse tree has a flat structure at this point with
3936 # the clauses being siblings of the contents of the clauses. The
3937 # final index in this list will hold the position of the end-select
3938 # statement.
3939 clause_indices = []
3940 selector = None
3941 # The position of the 'case default' clause, if any
3942 default_clause_idx = None
3943 for idx, child in enumerate(node.content):
3944 if isinstance(child, Fortran2003.Select_Case_Stmt):
3945 selector = child.items[0]
3946 if isinstance(child, Fortran2003.Case_Stmt):
3947 if not isinstance(child.items[0], Fortran2003.Case_Selector):
3948 raise InternalError(
3949 f"Unexpected parse tree structure. Expected child of "
3950 f"Case_Stmt to be a Case_Selector but got: "
3951 f"'{type(child.items[0]).__name__}'")
3952 case_expression = child.items[0].items[0]
3953 if case_expression is None:
3954 # This is a 'case default' clause - store its position.
3955 # We do this separately as this clause is special and
3956 # will be added as a final 'else'.
3957 default_clause_idx = idx
3958 clause_indices.append(idx)
3959 if isinstance(child, Fortran2003.End_Select_Stmt):
3960 clause_indices.append(idx)
3961
3962 # Deeply-nested ifblocks are problematic because they will exceed the
3963 # python recursion limits for some psyir analysis. These are not
3964 # typically found in input code, but select-case with a large number
3965 # of cases are more probable. If we find one of such cases we
3966 # preventively increase the python recursion limits.
3967 if len(clause_indices) > 150:
3968 # TODO #11: It would be good to log this
3969 sys.setrecursionlimit(len(clause_indices) * 10) # Default is 1000
3970
3971 # Deal with each Case_Stmt
3972 rootif = None
3973 currentparent = parent
3974 num_clauses = len(clause_indices) - 1
3975 for idx in range(num_clauses):
3976 # Skip the 'default' clause for now because we handle it last
3977 if clause_indices[idx] == default_clause_idx:
3978 continue
3979 start_idx = clause_indices[idx]
3980 end_idx = clause_indices[idx+1]
3981 clause = node.content[start_idx]
3982 case = clause.items[0]
3983

3986 if rootif:
3987 elsebody = Schedule(parent=currentparent)
3988 currentparent.addchild(elsebody)
3989 ifblock = IfBlock(annotations=['was_case'])
3990 elsebody.addchild(ifblock)
3991 elsebody.ast = node.content[start_idx + 1]
3992 elsebody.ast_end = node.content[end_idx - 1]
3993 else:
3994 ifblock = IfBlock(parent=currentparent,
3995 annotations=['was_case'])
3996 rootif = ifblock
3997
3998 if idx == 0:
3999 # If this is the first IfBlock then have it point to
4000 # the original SELECT CASE in the parse tree
4001 ifblock.ast = node
4002 else:
4003 # Otherwise, this IfBlock represents a CASE clause in the
4004 # Fortran and so we point to the parse tree of the content
4005 # of the clause.
4006 ifblock.ast = node.content[start_idx + 1]
4007 ifblock.ast_end = node.content[end_idx - 1]

4046 elsebody.ast_end = node.content[end_idx - 1]

5108 def _char_literal_handler(self, node, parent):
5109 '''
5110 Transforms an fparser2 character literal into a PSyIR literal.
5111 Currently does not support the use of a double '' or double "" to
5112 represent a single instance of one of those characters within a string
5113 delimited by the same character.
5114
5115 :param node: node in fparser2 parse tree.
5116 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Char_Literal_Constant`
5117 :param parent: parent node of the PSyIR node we are constructing.
5118 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
5119
5120 :returns: PSyIR representation of node.
5121 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Literal`
5122
5123 '''
5124 character_type = ScalarType(ScalarType.Intrinsic.CHARACTER,
5125 get_literal_precision(node, parent))
5126 # fparser issue #295 - the value of the character string currently
5127 # contains the quotation symbols themselves. Once that's fixed this
5128 # check will need to be changed.
5129 char_value = str(node.items[0])
5130 if not ((char_value.startswith("'") and char_value.endswith("'")) or
5131 (char_value.startswith('"') and char_value.endswith('"'))):
5132 raise InternalError(
5133 f"Char literal handler expects a quoted value but got: "
5134 f">>{char_value}<<")
5135 # In Fortran "x""x" or 'x''x' represents a string containing x"x
5136 # or x'x, respectively. (See Note 4.12 in the Fortran 2003 standard.)
5137 # However, checking whether we have e.g. 'that''s a cat''s mat' is
5138 # difficult and so, for now, we don't support it.
5139 if len(char_value) > 2 and ("''" in char_value or '""' in char_value):
5140 raise NotImplementedError("Unsupported Literal")
5141 # Strip the wrapping quotation chars before storing the value.
5142 return Literal(char_value[1:-1], character_type)

3129 def _create_bounded_loop(self, parent, variable, limits_list):
3130 '''
3131 Create a Loop instance with start, stop, step expressions.
3132
3133 :param parent: the parent of the node.
3134 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
3135 :param variable: the loop variable.
3136 :type variable: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataSymbol`
3137 :param limits_list: a list of fparser expressions reprsenting the
3138 loop bounds.
3139 :type limits_list: List[:py:class:`fparser.two.utils.Base`]
3140
3141 :return: a new Loop instance.
3142 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Loop`
3143
3144 '''
3145 # Loop variable must be a DataSymbol of integer type.
3146 variable_name = str(variable)
3147 data_symbol = _find_or_create_unresolved_symbol(
3148 parent, variable_name, symbol_type=DataSymbol,
3149 datatype=default_integer_type())
3150
3151 # The loop node is created with the _create_loop factory method as
3152 # some APIs require a specialised loop node type.
3153 loop = self._create_loop(parent, data_symbol)
3154
3155 # The Loop Limits are:
3156 # [start value expression, end value expression, step expression]
3157 self.process_nodes(parent=loop, nodes=[limits_list[0]])
3158 self.process_nodes(parent=loop, nodes=[limits_list[1]])
3159 if len(limits_list) == 3 and limits_list[2] is not None:
3160 self.process_nodes(parent=loop, nodes=[limits_list[2]])
3161 else:
3162 # Default loop increment is 1. Use the type of the start
3163 # or step nodes once #685 is complete. For the moment use
3164 # the default precision.
3165 default_step = Literal("1", default_integer_type())
3166 loop.addchild(default_step)
3167
3168 # Create Loop body Schedule
3169 loop_body = Schedule(parent=loop)
3170 loop.addchild(loop_body)
3171 return loop

3751 def _create_select_type_info(node):
3752 '''Create and return a SelectTypeInfo instance that stores the required
3753 information for a select-type construct to be used by
3754 subsequent methods.
3755
3756 :param node: fparser2 node from which to extract the select-type
3757 information.
3758 :type node: :py:class:`fparser2.Fortran2003.Select_Type_Construct`
3759
3760 :returns: instance of the SelectTypeInfo dataclass containing
3761 information about the select-type construct.
3762 :rtype: :py:class:`Self.SelectTypeInfo`
3763
3764 '''

3768 for child in node.children:
3769 if isinstance(child, Fortran2003.Select_Type_Stmt):
3770 # Found the select type stmt clause ('select type
3771 # (x)')
3772 if child.children[0]:
3773 # The selector variable ('x') is renamed and this
3774 # is not yet supported.
3775 raise NotImplementedError(
3776 f"The selector variable '{child.children[1]}' is "
3777 f"renamed to '{child.children[0]}' in the select "
3778 f"clause '{str(node)}'. This is not yet supported in "
3779 f"the PSyIR.")
3780 # Store the name of the selector variable in our
3781 # dataclass instance.

3784 # Found one of the type stmt guard clauses ('type is',
3785 # 'class is', or 'class default').
3786 select_idx += 1
3787 select_type.stmts.append([])
3788 # Extract the fparser2 Type_Specification
3789 # e.g. 'real(kind=4)'
3790 type_spec = child.children[1]

3792 intrinsic_base_name = None
3793 if type_spec is None:
3794 # There is no type information so this is the
3795 # default clause
3796 type_name = None
3797 elif isinstance(type_spec, Fortran2003.Intrinsic_Type_Spec):
3798 # The guard type selector is an intrinsic type
3799 # e.g. 'type is(REAL)'. Set the intrinsic base name
3800 # as there is a base intrinsic type.

3802 # Determine type_name for all the different cases

3173 def _deallocate_handler(self, node, parent):
3174 '''
3175 Transforms a deallocate() statement into its PSyIR form.
3176
3177 :param node: node in fparser2 tree.
3178 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Deallocate_Stmt`
3179 :param parent: parent node of the PSyIR node we are constructing.
3180 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Schedule`
3181
3182 :returns: PSyIR for a deallocate.
3183 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.IntrinsicCall`
3184
3185 '''
3186 call = IntrinsicCall(
3187 IntrinsicCall.Intrinsic.DEALLOCATE, parent=parent)
3188 dealloc_list = node.children[0].children
3189 for dealloc in dealloc_list:
3190 self.process_nodes(parent=call, nodes=[dealloc])
3191
3192 # Handle any options to the deallocate()
3193 opt_list = walk(node, Fortran2003.Dealloc_Opt)
3194 for opt in opt_list:
3195 self.process_nodes(parent=call, nodes=opt.children[1:])
3196 call.append_named_arg(opt.children[0], call.children[-1].detach())
3197
3198 # Point to the original statement in the parse tree.
3199 call.ast = node
3200
3201 return call

3204 '''
3205 Transforms a fparser2 Do Construct into its PSyIR form.
3206
3207 :param node: node in fparser2 tree.
3208 :type node: \
3209 :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Block_Nonlabel_Do_Construct`
3210 :param parent: parent node of the PSyIR node we are constructing.
3211 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
3212
3213 :returns: PSyIR representation of node
3214 :rtype: Union[:py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Loop`, \
3215 :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.WhileLoop`]
3216
3217 :raises NotImplementedError: if the fparser2 tree has a named DO \
3218 containing a reference to that name.

3220 nonlabel_do = walk(node.content, Fortran2003.Nonlabel_Do_Stmt)[0]
3221 if nonlabel_do.item is not None:
3222 # If the associated line has a name that is referenced inside the
3223 # loop then it isn't supported , e.g. `EXIT outer_loop`.
3224 if nonlabel_do.item.name:
3225 construct_name = nonlabel_do.item.name
3226 # Check that the construct-name is not referred to inside
3227 # the Loop (but exclude the END DO from this check).

3231 "Unsupported label reference within DO")

3235 # types children None is not None, this one defines the loop boundaries

3311 def _if_construct_handler(self, node, parent):
3312 '''
3313 Transforms an fparser2 If_Construct to the PSyIR representation.
3314
3315 :param node: node in fparser2 tree.
3316 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.If_Construct`

3319 :returns: PSyIR representation of node

3322 structure.

3324
3325 # Check that the fparser2 parsetree has the expected structure
3326 if len(walk(node, Fortran2003.If_Then_Stmt)) == 0:
3327 raise InternalError(
3328 f"Failed to find opening if then statement in: {node}")
3329 if len(walk(node, Fortran2003.End_If_Stmt)) == 0:
3330 raise InternalError(
3331 f"Failed to find closing end if statement in: {node}")
3332

3336 if isinstance(child, (Fortran2003.If_Then_Stmt,
3337 Fortran2003.Else_Stmt,
3338 Fortran2003.Else_If_Stmt,
3339 Fortran2003.End_If_Stmt)):

3341
3342 # Get the comments before the 'if' statement
3343 preceding_comments = []

3345 if isinstance(child, Fortran2003.Comment):
3346 self.process_comment(child, preceding_comments)
3347 # NOTE: The comments are added to the IfBlock node.
3348 # NOTE: Comments before the 'else[if]' statements are not handled.
3349
3350 # Deal with each clause: "if", "else if" or "else".

3352 currentparent = parent

3354 for idx in range(num_clauses):
3355 start_idx = clause_indices[idx]
3356 end_idx = clause_indices[idx+1]
3357 clause = node.content[start_idx]

3360 Fortran2003.Else_If_Stmt)):

3362 # it is an 'ELSE' clause and it needs an IfBlock annotated
3363 # with 'was_elseif' inside a Schedule.

3365 if isinstance(clause, Fortran2003.If_Then_Stmt):
3366 ifblock = IfBlock(parent=currentparent)
3367 ifblock.ast = node # Keep pointer to fpaser2 AST
3368 newifblock = ifblock
3369 else:
3370 elsebody = Schedule(parent=currentparent)
3371 currentparent.addchild(elsebody)
3372 newifblock = IfBlock(parent=elsebody,
3373 annotations=['was_elseif'])
3374 elsebody.addchild(newifblock)

3376 # Keep pointer to fpaser2 AST

3378 newifblock.ast = node.content[start_idx]
3379
3380 # Add the comments to the if block.
3381 newifblock.preceding_comment\
3382 = self._comments_list_to_string(preceding_comments)
3383 preceding_comments = []
3384
3385 # Create condition as first child
3386 self.process_nodes(parent=newifblock,

3392 ifbody.ast_end = node.content[end_idx - 1]
3393 newifblock.addchild(ifbody)
3394 self.process_nodes(parent=ifbody,
3395 nodes=node.content[start_idx + 1:end_idx])
3396
3397 currentparent = newifblock

5093 get_literal_precision(node, parent))

1200 def _parse_dimensions(self, dimensions, symbol_table):
1201 '''
1202 Parse the fparser dimension attribute into a shape list. Each entry of
1203 this list is either None (if the extent is unknown) or a 2-tuple
1204 containing the lower and upper bound of that dimension.
1205
1206 :param dimensions: fparser dimension attribute.
1207 :type dimensions:
1208 :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Dimension_Attr_Spec`
1209 :param symbol_table: symbol table of the declaration context.
1210 :type symbol_table: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.SymbolTable`
1211
1212 :returns: shape of the attribute in column-major order (leftmost
1213 index is contiguous in memory). Each entry represents an array
1214 dimension. If it is 'None' the extent of that dimension is
1215 unknown, otherwise it holds a 2-tuple with the upper and lower
1216 bounds of the dimension. If it is an empty list then the symbol
1217 represents a scalar.
1218 :rtype: list[Optional[
1219 tuple[:py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.DataNode`,
1220 :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.DataNode`]]]
1221
1222 :raises GenerationError: if invalid Fortran is encounted in the
1223 dimensions list.
1224 :raises NotImplementedError: if the supplied dimension represents an
1225 assumed-size specification.
1226 :raises InternalError: if a dimension is not an Assumed_Shape_Spec,
1227 Explicit_Shape_Spec or Assumed_Size_Spec.
1228
1229 '''
1230 one = Literal("1", INTEGER_TYPE)
1231 shape = []
1232 # Traverse shape specs in Depth-first-search order
1233 for dim in walk(dimensions, (Fortran2003.Assumed_Shape_Spec,
1234 Fortran2003.Deferred_Shape_Spec,
1235 Fortran2003.Explicit_Shape_Spec,
1236 Fortran2003.Assumed_Size_Spec)):

1239 # Assumed_Shape_Spec has two children holding the lower and
1240 # upper bounds. It is valid Fortran (R514) to specify only the
1241 # lower bound:
1242 # ":" -> Assumed_Shape_Spec(None, None)
1243 # "4:" -> Assumed_Shape_Spec(Int_Literal_Constant('4', None),
1244 # None)
1245 lower = None
1246 if dim.children[0]:
1247 lower = self._process_array_bound(dim.children[0],
1248 symbol_table)
1249 if dim.children[1]:
1250 upper = self._process_array_bound(dim.children[1],
1251 symbol_table)
1252 else:
1253 upper = ArrayType.Extent.ATTRIBUTE if lower else None
1254
1255 if upper and not lower:

1257 f"Found an assumed-shape array declaration with only "
1258 f"an upper bound ({dimensions}). This is not valid "
1259 f"Fortran.")

1262 else:

1272 symbol_table)

1275 symbol_table)
1276 shape.append((lower, upper))

The optional canonicalise function allows the order of the

form has all required arguments as positional arguments and
all optional arguments as named arguments, which would result
in sum(a, dim=dim, mask=mask) in this case.

5215 '''Processes fparser2 call or intrinsic arguments contained in the
5216 node argument and adds them to the PSyIR Call or IntrinsicCall
5217 contained in the call argument, respectively.
5218
5219 The optional canonicalise function allows the order of the
5220 call's arguments and its named arguments to be re-ordered and
5221 modified to a canonical form so that the PSyIR does not need
5222 to support the different forms that are allowed in
5223 Fortran.
5224
5225 For example, both sum(a, dim, mask) and sum(dim=dim,
5226 mask=mask, array=a) are equivalant in Fortran. The canonical
5227 form has all required arguments as positional arguments and
5228 all optional arguments as named arguments, which would result
5229 in sum(a, dim=dim, mask=mask) in this case.
5230
5231 :param node: an fparser call node representing a call or \
5232 an intrinsic call.
5233 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Call_Stmt` or \
5234 :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Intrinsic_Function_Reference`
5235 :param call: a PSyIR call argument representing a call or an \
5236 intrinsic call.
5237 :type call: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Call` or \
5238 :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.IntrinsicCall`
5239 :param function canonicalise: a function that canonicalises \
5240 the call arguments.
5241
5242 :returns: the PSyIR call argument with the PSyIR \
5243 representation of the fparser2 node arguments.
5244 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Call` or \
5245 :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.IntrinsicCall`
5246
5247 :raises GenerationError: if all named arguments do not follow \
5248 all positional arguments.
5249

5252 arg_names = []

5254 # Store the names of any named args

5256

5258 # arguments. This should be the case but fparser does not
5259 # currently check and this ordering is assumed by the
5260 # canonicalise function. LFRic invokes can cause this
5261 # exception (as they often use name=xxx before the end of the
5262 # argument list), so to avoid this we only check when a
5263 # canonicalise function is supplied (which we know is not the
5264 # case for invokes as they are calls).

5268 index += 1

5273 f"positional arguments, but found '{node}'.")

5276 # re-orders arg_nodes and renames arg_names appropriately for
5277 # the particular call to make a canonical version. This is
5278 # required because intrinsics can be written with and without
5279 # named arguments (or combinations thereof) in Fortran.

5286 # names

5291 call.append_named_arg(arg_names[idx], child)

5294 call.ast = node

protected 
Processes the supplied list of fparser2 nodes representing case-value
expressions and constructs the equivalent PSyIR representation.
e.g. for:

       SELECT CASE(my_flag)
       CASE(var1, var2:var3, :var5)
         my_switch = .true.
       END SELECT

the equivalent logical expression is:

my_flag == var1 OR (myflag>=var2 AND myflag <= var3) OR my_flag <= var5

and the corresponding structure of the PSyIR that we create is:

            OR
           /  \
         EQ    OR
              /  \
           AND    LE
          /  \
        GE    LE

:param selector: the fparser2 parse tree representing the \

:type selector: sub-class of :py:class:`fparser.two.utils.Base`
:param nodes: the nodes representing the label-list of the current \

:type nodes: list of :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Name` or \
             :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Case_Value_Range`
:param parent: parent node in the PSyIR.

2656 def _process_data_statements(nodes, psyir_parent):
2657 '''Limited support for data statements: they will be converted
2658 to UnsupportedFortranTypes, and added to the symbol table
2659 using an internal PSyclone name. The complexity of data
2660 statements come from implicit loops, e.g.:
2661 DATA (es(ies),ies = 0, 5) / 0.966483e-02,... /
2662
2663 :param nodes: fparser2 AST nodes containing declaration statements.
2664 :type nodes: List[:py:class:`fparser.two.utils.Base`]
2665 :param psyir_parent: the PSyIR Node with a symbol table in which to
2666 add the data statements and update the interfaces of the symbols
2667 used in the data statement.
2668 :type psyir_parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.ScopingNode`
2669 '''
2670
2671 # Traverse the tree, and find all Data_Stmt_Object_Lists, which
2672 # contain the variables defined in the data statement.
2673 for data_stmt in walk(nodes, Fortran2003.Data_Stmt):
2674 # Add the data statement as a special symbol to the symbol
2675 # table, so the backend can recreate the data statement
2676 psyir_parent.symbol_table.new_symbol(
2677 root_name="_PSYCLONE_INTERNAL_DATA_STMT",
2678 symbol_type=DataSymbol,
2679 datatype=UnsupportedFortranType(str(data_stmt)))
2680 # Each Data_Stmt_Object_List contains either a variable
2681 # (which is a Name or PartRef), or a (potentially nested)
2682 # implied do loop ... which at the end will have an array_element
2683 # or a scalar_structure_component.
2684 # Collect all the variable names in a set
2685 all_vars = set()
2686 # Now find all variable (directly, or in implied do loops):
2687 for data_obj in walk(data_stmt, Fortran2003.Data_Stmt_Object_List):
2688 for var_or_implied_do in data_obj.children:
2689 # Check for implied do loops first. In case
2690 if isinstance(var_or_implied_do,
2691 Fortran2003.Data_Implied_Do):
2692 for part_ref in walk(var_or_implied_do,
2693 Fortran2003.Part_Ref):
2694 all_vars.add(str(part_ref.children[0]))
2695 elif isinstance(var_or_implied_do, Fortran2003.Name):
2696 # No implied do loop, just a name:
2697 all_vars.add(str(var_or_implied_do))
2698 else:
2699 # Now must be Data_Ref. Get the var name:
2700 name = var_or_implied_do.children[0]
2701 all_vars.add(str(name))
2702
2703 # Variables in a data statement have an implied static attribute.
2704 # Add this explicit:
2705 for var_name in all_vars:
2706 try:
2707 sym = psyir_parent.symbol_table.lookup(var_name)
2708 except KeyError:
2709 sym = _find_or_create_unresolved_symbol(
2710 psyir_parent, var_name, symbol_type=DataSymbol,
2711 datatype=UnresolvedType())
2712 sym.interface = StaticInterface()

2266 '''
2267 Processes a Fortran2003.Interface_Block. If the interface is named
2268 and consists only of [module] procedure :: <procedure-list> then a
2269 GenericInterfaceSymbol is created. Otherwise, a RoutineSymbol of
2270 UnsupportedFortranType is created.
2271
2272 :param node: the parse tree for the interface block.
2273 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Interface_Block`

2275 :type symbol_table: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.SymbolTable`

2279 str, :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol.Visibility`]

2282 # Fortran 2003 standard R1203 says that:
2283 # interface-stmt is INTERFACE [ generic-spec ]
2284 # or ABSTRACT INTERFACE

2286 # of OPERATOR, ASSIGNMENT or dtio-spec.

2288 Fortran2003.Name):

2290 # RoutineSymbol with an internal name and with the content of the
2291 # interface being kept within an UnsupportedFortranType. As a
2292 # result the visibility and interface details of the RoutineSymbol
2293 # do not matter.
2294 symbol_table.new_symbol(
2295 root_name="_psyclone_internal_interface",
2296 symbol_type=RoutineSymbol,
2297 datatype=UnsupportedFortranType(str(node).lower()))

2303 name, symbol_table.default_visibility)

1401 UnsupportedFortranType being added to the symbol table associated with
1402 `parent`.

1404 :param nodes: nodes in the fparser2 parse tree describing a
1405 Specification Part that will be searched.
1406 :type nodes: List[:py:class:`fparser.two.utils.Base`]
1407 :param : the parent node in the PSyIR under construction.
1408 :type : :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`

1410 :returns: names of symbols that are static or just "*" if they all are.
1411 :rtype: List[str]

1414 without a saved-entity list *and* one or more SAVE attributes or
1415 SAVE statements (C580).

1421 # via an explicit SAVE stmt (e.g. "SAVE :: my_var")

1433 stmt.children[1].children]

1438 # This should really be caught by the Fortran parser but
1439 # fparser2 is lax.

1443 f"list plus one or more SAVES *with* saved-entity lists "
1444 f"(naming {names}). This is not valid Fortran.")

1618 :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Declaration_Type_Spec`

1621 :rtype: 2-tuple of :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.ScalarType` or \
1622 :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataTypeSymbol` and \

1460 def _process_use_stmts(self, parent, nodes, visibility_map=None):
1461 '''
1462 Process all of the USE statements in the fparser2 parse tree
1463 supplied as a list of nodes. Imported symbols are added to
1464 the symbol table associated with the supplied parent node with
1465 Import interfaces.
1466
1467 :param parent: PSyIR node in which to insert the symbols found.
1468 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.KernelSchedule`

1470 :type nodes: list of :py:class:`fparser.two.utils.Base`
1471 :param visibility_map: mapping of symbol name to visibility (for \
1472 those symbols listed in an accessibility statement).
1473 :type visibility_map: dict with str keys and \
1474 :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol.Visibility` values
1475
1476 :raises GenerationError: if the parse tree for a use statement has an \
1477 unrecognised structure.
1478 :raises SymbolError: if a symbol imported via a use statement is \
1479 already present in the symbol table.
1480 :raises NotImplementedError: if the form of use statement is not \

1485 visibility_map = {}

5644 def _program_handler(self, node, parent):
5645 '''Processes an fparser2 Program statement. Program is the top level
5646 node of a complete fparser2 tree and may contain one or more
5647 program-units. This is captured with a FileContainer node.
5648
5649 :param node: top level node in fparser2 parse tree.
5650 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Program`
5651 :param parent: parent node of the PSyIR node we are constructing.
5652 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
5653
5654 :returns: PSyIR representation of the program.
5655 :rtype: subclass of :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
5656
5657 '''
5658 # fparser2 does not keep the original filename (if there was
5659 # one) so this can't be provided as the name of the
5660 # FileContainer.
5661 file_container = FileContainer("None", parent=parent)
5662 if len(node.children) == 1 and node.children[0] is None:
5663 # We have an empty file
5664 return file_container
5665 self.process_nodes(file_container, node.children)
5666 return file_container

3845 def _select_type_construct_handler(self, node, parent):
3846 '''
3847 Transforms an fparser2 Select_Type_Construct to the PSyIR
3848 representation (consisting of an Assignment, a CodeBlock
3849 and an IfBlock).
3850
3851 :param node: node in fparser2 tree.
3852 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Select_Type_Construct`
3853 :param parent: parent node of the PSyIR node we are constructing.
3854 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
3855
3856 :returns: PSyIR representation of the node.
3857 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.IfBlock`
3858
3859 :raises NotImplementedError: if the symbol representing the type-
3860 selector variable is not resolved or is not a DataSymbol.
3861
3862 '''
3863 # Step 1: Search for all the TYPE IS and CLASS IS clauses in
3864 # the Select_Type_Construct and extract the required
3865 # information. This makes for easier code generation later in
3866 # the routine.
3867 insert_index = len(parent.children) - 1
3868 # Create the required type information in a dataclass instance.
3869 select_type = self._create_select_type_info(node)
3870
3871 # We don't immediately add our new nodes into the PSyIR tree in
3872 # case we encounter something we don't support (in which case
3873 # an exception will be raised and a CodeBlock created).
3874 tmp_parent = Schedule(parent=parent)
3875
3876 # Step 2: Recreate the select type clause within a CodeBlock
3877 # with the content of the clauses being replaced by a string
3878 # capturing the name of the type or class clauses
3879 # ('type_string'). The string symbol is returned for use in
3880 # step 3, as is the list of any pointers to the selector variable.
3881 # TODO #2550 - use an integer instead of a string to encode
3882 # which branch is chosen at run-time.
3883 type_string_symbol, pointer_symbols = self._create_select_type(
3884 tmp_parent, select_type, type_string_name="type_string")
3885
3886 # Step 3: Create the (potentially nested) if statement that
3887 # replicates the content of the select type options (as select
3888 # type is not supported directly in the PSyIR) allowing the
3889 # PSyIR to 'see' the select type content.
3890 outer_ifblock = self._create_ifblock_for_select_type_content(
3891 parent, select_type, type_string_symbol, pointer_symbols)
3892
3893 # Step 4: Ensure that the type selector variable declaration
3894 # has the pointer or target attribute as we need to create
3895 # pointers that point to it to get the specific type.
3896 self._add_target_attribute(select_type.selector,
3897 outer_ifblock.scope.symbol_table)
3898
3899 # Step 5: We didn't encounter any problems so finally attach our new
3900 # nodes to the PSyIR tree in the location we saved earlier.
3901 for child in reversed(tmp_parent.pop_all_children()):
3902 parent.addchild(child, index=insert_index)
3903 # Ensure any Symbols are moved over too.
3904 parent.scope.symbol_table.merge(tmp_parent.symbol_table)
3905
3906 return outer_ifblock

4688 methods respectively), and Data_Pointer_Object (representing an access

4692 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Data_Ref` |
4693 :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Process_Designator` |
4694 :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Data_Pointer_Object`

4696 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`

4698 :return: PSyIR representation of node
4699 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.StructureReference` |
4700 :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.ArrayOfStructuresReference`
4701
4702 :raises NotImplementedError: if the parse tree contains unsupported
4703 elements.
4704

4721 # implementation easier because its the same as procedure-designator)

5299 '''Transforms an fparser2 Subroutine_Subprogram or Function_Subprogram
5300 statement into a PSyIR Routine node.

5303 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Subroutine_Subprogram`
5304 or :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Function_Subprogram`

4996 def _subscript_triplet_handler(self, node, parent):
4997 '''
4998 Transforms an fparser2 Subscript_Triplet to the PSyIR
4999 representation.
5000
5001 :param node: node in fparser2 AST.
5002 :type node: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Subscript_Triplet`
5003 :param parent: parent node of the PSyIR node we are constructing.
5004 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
5005
5006 :returns: PSyIR of fparser2 node.
5007 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Range`
5008
5009 :raises InternalError: if the supplied parent node is not a sub-class \
5010 of either Reference or Member.
5011 '''
5012 # The PSyIR stores array dimension information for the ArrayMixin
5013 # class in an ordered list. As we are processing the
5014 # dimensions in order, the number of children already added to
5015 # our parent indicates the current array dimension being processed
5016 # (with 0 being the first dimension, 1 being the second etc). Fortran
5017 # specifies the 1st dimension as being 1, the second dimension being
5018 # 2, etc.). We therefore add 1 to the number of children already added
5019 # to our parent to determine the Fortran dimension value. However, we
5020 # do have to take care in case the parent is a member of a structure
5021 # rather than a plain array reference.
5022 if isinstance(parent, (Reference, Member)):
5023 dimension = str(len([kid for kid in parent.children if
5024 not isinstance(kid, Member)]) + 1)
5025 else:
5026 raise InternalError(
5027 f"Expected parent PSyIR node to be either a Reference or a "
5028 f"Member but got '{type(parent).__name__}' when processing "
5029 f"'{node}'")
5030
5031 integer_type = default_integer_type()
5032 my_range = Range(parent=parent)
5033 my_range.children = []
5034
5035 if node.children[0]:
5036 self.process_nodes(parent=my_range, nodes=[node.children[0]])
5037 else:
5038 # There is no lower bound, it is implied. This is not
5039 # supported in the PSyIR so we create the equivalent code
5040 # by using the PSyIR lbound intrinsic function:
5041 # a(:...) becomes a(lbound(a,1):...)
5042 lbound = IntrinsicCall.create(
5043 IntrinsicCall.Intrinsic.LBOUND,
5044 [_copy_full_base_reference(parent),
5045 ("dim", Literal(dimension, integer_type))])
5046 my_range.children.append(lbound)
5047
5048 if node.children[1]:
5049 self.process_nodes(parent=my_range, nodes=[node.children[1]])
5050 else:
5051 # There is no upper bound, it is implied. This is not
5052 # supported in the PSyIR so we create the equivalent code
5053 # by using the PSyIR ubound intrinsic function:
5054 # a(...:) becomes a(...:ubound(a,1))
5055 ubound = IntrinsicCall.create(
5056 IntrinsicCall.Intrinsic.UBOUND,
5057 [_copy_full_base_reference(parent),
5058 ("dim", Literal(dimension, integer_type))])
5059 my_range.children.append(ubound)
5060
5061 if node.children[2]:
5062 self.process_nodes(parent=my_range, nodes=[node.children[2]])
5063 else:
5064 # There is no step, it is implied. This is not
5065 # supported in the PSyIR so we create the equivalent code
5066 # by using a PSyIR integer literal with the value 1
5067 # a(...:...:) becomes a(...:...:1)
5068 literal = Literal("1", integer_type)
5069 my_range.children.append(literal)
5070 return my_range

1048 def nodes_to_code_block(parent, fp2_nodes, message=None):
1049 '''Create a CodeBlock for the supplied list of fparser2 nodes and then
1050 wipe the list. A CodeBlock is a node in the PSyIR (Schedule)
1051 that represents a sequence of one or more Fortran statements
1052 and/or expressions which PSyclone does not attempt to handle.
1053
1054 :param parent: Node in the PSyclone AST to which to add this CodeBlock.
1055 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
1056 :param fp2_nodes: list of fparser2 AST nodes constituting the
1057 CodeBlock.
1058 :type fp2_nodes: list of :py:class:`fparser.two.utils.Base`
1059 :param message: Include a preceeding comment attached to the CodeBlock.
1060 :type message: Optional[str]

1062 :returns: a CodeBlock instance.
1063 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.CodeBlock`
1064
1065 '''
1066 if not fp2_nodes:
1067 return None
1068
1069 # Determine whether this code block is a statement or an
1070 # expression. Statements always have a `Schedule` as parent
1071 # and expressions do not. The only unknown at this point are
1072 # directives whose structure are in discussion. Therefore, for
1073 # the moment, an exception is raised if a directive is found
1074 # as a parent.
1075 if isinstance(parent, (Schedule, Container)):
1076 structure = CodeBlock.Structure.STATEMENT

1079 "Fparser2Reader:nodes_to_code_block: A CodeBlock with "

1085 if message:

1087 parent.addchild(code_block)
1088 del fp2_nodes[:]

1294 def process_access_statements(nodes):
1295 '''
1296 Search the supplied list of fparser2 nodes (which must represent a
1297 complete Specification Part) for any accessibility
1298 statements (e.g. "PUBLIC :: my_var") to determine the default
1299 visibility of symbols as well as identifying those that are
1300 explicitly declared as public or private.
1301
1302 :param nodes: nodes in the fparser2 parse tree describing a \
1303 Specification Part that will be searched.
1304 :type nodes: list of :py:class:`fparser.two.utils.Base`
1305
1306 :returns: default visibility of symbols within the current scoping \
1307 unit and dict of symbol names with explicit visibilities.
1308 :rtype: 2-tuple of (:py:class:`psyclone.symbols.Symbol.Visibility`, \
1309 dict)
1310
1311 :raises InternalError: if an accessibility attribute which is not \
1312 'public' or 'private' is encountered.
1313 :raises GenerationError: if the parse tree is found to contain more \
1314 than one bare accessibility statement (i.e. 'PUBLIC' or 'PRIVATE')
1315 :raises GenerationError: if a symbol is explicitly declared as being \
1316 both public and private.
1317
1318 '''
1319 default_visibility = None
1320 # Sets holding the names of those symbols whose access is specified
1321 # explicitly via an access-stmt (e.g. "PUBLIC :: my_var")
1322 explicit_public = set()
1323 explicit_private = set()

1325 # of a *module*.

1332 elif stmt.children[0].lower() == "private":

1334 else:
1335 raise InternalError(

1337 f"attribute of '{stmt.children[0]}' but expected either "
1338 f"'public' or 'private'.")

1341 # We've already seen an access statement without an
1342 # access-id-list. This is therefore invalid Fortran (which
1343 # fparser does not catch).

1349 raise GenerationError(

5695 def process_comment(self, comment, preceding_comments):
5696 '''
5697 Process a comment and attach it to the last PSyIR object (Symbol or
5698 Node) if it is an inline comment. Otherwise append it to the
5699 preceding_comments list. Ignore empty comments.
5700
5701 :param comment: Comment to process.
5702 :type comment: :py:class:`fparser.two.utils.Comment`
5703 :param preceding_comments: List of comments that precede the next node.
5704 :type preceding_comments: List[:py:class:`fparser.two.utils.Comment`]
5705
5706 '''
5707 if len(comment.tostr()) == 0:
5708 return
5709 if self._ignore_directives and comment.tostr().startswith("!$"):
5710 return
5711 if self._last_psyir_parsed_and_span is not None:
5712 last_psyir, last_span = self._last_psyir_parsed_and_span
5713 if (last_span[1] is not None
5714 and last_span[1] == comment.item.span[0]):
5715 last_psyir.inline_comment = self._comment_to_string(comment)
5716 return

5718 preceding_comments.append(comment)

psyclone.psyir.frontend.fparser2.Fparser2Reader.process_declarations ( self,
parent,

Transform the variable declarations in the fparser2 parse tree into
symbols in the symbol table of the PSyIR parent node. The default
visibility of any new symbol is taken from the symbol table associated
with the `parent` node if necessary. The `visibility_map` provides
information on any explicit symbol visibilities that are specified
for the declarations.

:param parent: PSyIR node in which to insert the symbols found.
:type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.KernelSchedule`
:param nodes: fparser2 AST nodes containing declaration statements.
:type nodes: List[:py:class:`fparser.two.utils.Base`]
:param arg_list: fparser2 AST node containing the argument list.
:type arg_list: :py:class:`fparser.Fortran2003.Dummy_Arg_List`
:param visibility_map: mapping of symbol names to explicit
    visibilities.
:type visibility_map: dict[
    str, :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol.Visibility`]

:raises GenerationError: if an INCLUDE statement is encountered.
:raises NotImplementedError: the provided declarations contain
    attributes which are not supported yet.
:raises GenerationError: if the parse tree for a USE statement does
    not have the expected structure.
:raises SymbolError: if a declaration is found for a Symbol that is
    already in the symbol table with a defined interface.
:raises InternalError: if the provided declaration is an unexpected
    or invalid fparser or Fortran expression.
